BiblicalUsage: Na'aman is pleasantness, and its only occurrence turns the word into a warning. In Isaiah 17:10 the people have forgotten the God of their salvation, so they plant pleasant plants and set strange slips, tending a garden while forgetting the Rock of their strength.
TheologicalSignificance: I believe pleasant things make a poor substitute for the God who saves; a garden planted in forgetfulness is still a garden, but it will not hold.
